problems.title: Nested decimal arithmetic
problems.question: Evaluate (2.4-(0.3-3.21)·2+0.44÷(-2))÷0.4.
problems.idea: Compute the inner difference and division first.
steps: Inside the outer parentheses: 2.4+5.82-0.22=8.
Divide by 0.4 to get 20.

problems.title: Order using signs and magnitude bounds
problems.question: The order is -1<a<0<1<b. Order a/b,1/a,b-a increasingly.
problems.idea: Find a separate interval for each expression.
steps: Reciprocating a number between -1 and 0 gives a number below -1.
Dividing negative a by b>1 makes it closer to zero.
The difference b-a is positive.

problems.title: Cost is proportional to bulb-hours
problems.question: Six identical bulbs cost 3 tetri to run for 7 hours. How many cost 4 tetri for 8 hours?
problems.idea: Compare total bulb-hours.
steps: If the bulb count is n, the cost is 8n/14.
Set 8n/14=4 to obtain n=7.

problems.title: Subtract perimeters with a shared side
problems.question: D lies on AB. Perimeters ABC=25,ACD=20 and CD=5. Find perimeter BCD.
problems.idea: Subtract the smaller triangle’s boundary lengths.
steps: The subtraction removes AC and leaves DB+BC-CD.
Add 2CD to obtain DB+BC+CD.
Numerically this is 25-20+10=15.

problems.title: Bisector and altitude split the angle differently
problems.question: In an acute triangle, two angles differ by 40°. Find the angle between the bisector and altitude from the third vertex.
problems.idea: Their deviation is half the difference of the two base angles.
steps: The altitude makes angles 90°-A and 90°-B with the two sides.
The bisector lies halfway between those sides, so it differs from the altitude by half their difference.
Thus the answer is 40°/2=20°.

problems.title: Perpendicular median and bisector
problems.question: AM is a median and BK an angle bisector in ABC, with AM⊥BK. AB=12. Find BC.
problems.idea: Place the B-bisector horizontally.
formulas: A=(c cosθ,c sinθ),C=(a cosθ,-a sinθ), where c=BA,a=BC and 0<θ<90°.
steps: The midpoint M of BC has horizontal coordinate a cosθ/2.
AM is vertical because it is perpendicular to the bisector. Hence A and M have equal horizontal coordinates.
Thus c cosθ=a cosθ/2, giving a=2c=24.

problems.title: Symmetric difference of size one toggles one element
problems.question: A has n elements and B⊂A has m elements. How many X⊆A satisfy |B△X|=1?
problems.idea: Choose the unique element whose membership changes.
steps: There are m ways to remove one element of B and n-m ways to add one from outside B.
The total is m+(n-m)=n.

problems.title: The greatest of several negative quantities
problems.question: a<-1<b<0<c<1<d. Which is greatest among ac,bc,ad,bd,a,b?
problems.idea: Multiplying a negative number by 0<c<1 moves it toward zero.
formulas: bc>b; bc>ac because b>a; bd<b because d>1.
steps: Also ac>a and ad<a, while a<b.
Combining the comparisons puts every other listed value below bc.

problems.title: Drawing scale versus actual size
problems.question: A wing is 15 cm long in a drawing at scale 50:1. Find its actual length.
problems.idea: The drawing is 50 times the real size.
steps: This is 0.3 cm, or 3 mm.

problems.title: A return journey closes the remaining gap
problems.question: Two cars leave together on a 432 km route at speeds in ratio 7:5. The faster turns back immediately at the destination. How far from it do they meet?
problems.idea: At the meeting their distances travelled are D+x and D-x.
steps: Cross-multiply: 5D+5x=7D-7x.
Thus 12x=2D and x=432/6=72.

problems.title: The smaller clock angle can repeat near either alignment
problems.question: The clock hands make the same smaller angle α now and 8 minutes ago. Find α.
problems.idea: Their relative motion is 5.5° per minute.
steps: The signed separation can change from -22° to +22°, giving α=22°.
It can also change from 158° to 202°; both have smaller angle 158°.
These exhaust 0≤α≤180° because 2α is congruent to ±44° modulo 360°.
problems.note: Only 22° is printed. Without a condition that the hands pass through alignment rather than opposition, 158° is also valid.

problems.title: Least integer above a rational root
problems.question: Find the least integer greater than the root of x/2+x/3+x/6=33/8.
problems.idea: The three coefficients add to 1.
steps: The least greater integer is 5.

problems.title: Appending a digit forms a new linear expression
problems.question: Appending 9 to natural n increases it by 180. How many positive divisors has the new number?
problems.idea: Appending a digit multiplies by 10 before adding it.
steps: 9n=171, so n=19 and the new number is 199.
199 is prime: none of 2,3,5,7,11,13 divides it, and these cover primes up to √199.
A prime has exactly two positive divisors.

problems.title: Angles inversely proportional to three integers
problems.question: Triangle angles are inversely proportional to 2,3,6. Find the largest.
problems.idea: Use reciprocal ratios.
steps: The six ratio units sum to 180°, so a unit is 30°.
The largest angle is 3·30°=90°.

problems.title: The specified isosceles angle can be apex or base
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has two angles 70° and x°. Find the sum of all distinct possible x.
problems.idea: Consider both roles for 70°.
formulas: Triangle angle sum=180°; two base angles are equal.
steps: If 70° is the apex, the others are 55°, so x=55°.
If 70° is a base angle, the other angles are 70°,40°, so x=70° or 40°.
The distinct values sum to 55+70+40=165.

problems.title: Two small isosceles triangles at an obtuse vertex
problems.question: In ABC, B=120°. D,E∈AC satisfy BD=AD and BE=EC. Find DBE.
problems.idea: Use equal-side base angles on both sides.
steps: The angle between BD and BE is B-A-C.

problems.title: Two internal divisions of the same segment
problems.question: C,D∈AB satisfy AC:BC=1:2 and AD:BD=2:3. Find AC:CD:DB.
problems.idea: Use AB as a common unit.
steps: Take AB=15 units, giving AC=5 and AD=6.
Then CD=1 and DB=9.

problems.title: Reflect a vertex across a median midpoint
problems.question: AD is a median and is extended to E with DE=AD. Given C=50°,B=70°, find ACE.
problems.idea: The diagonals of ABEC bisect each other.
formulas: D is the midpoint of both AE and BC, so ABEC is a parallelogram.
steps: Thus CE is parallel to AB in the same direction.
The angle between CA and CE is the supplement of A: 120°.

problems.title: A second jug changes the total to three original volumes
problems.question: Adding one jug of pure water changes a 10% salt solution to 5%. What happens after one more equal jug?
problems.idea: The first jug doubled the volume, so it equals the original solution volume.
steps: Let the original volume be V, containing 0.1V salt.
After two jugs the total volume is 3V.
The concentration is 0.1V/(3V)=1/30=3⅓%.

problems.title: Absolute value after signed multiplication
problems.question: Evaluate |5·(-3)-(-2)·4|.
problems.idea: Perform multiplication before subtraction.
steps: The inner value is -15-(-8)=-7.
Its absolute value is 7.

problems.title: An auxiliary isosceles triangle finds a side difference
problems.question: B=20°,C=40° and the A-bisector AD=24. Find BC-AB.
problems.idea: Choose E on BC with BE=AB.
formulas: Equal sides give equal opposite angles; A=120° and BAD=DAC=60°.
steps: Triangle ABE is isosceles with B=20°, so BAE=AEB=80°. The ray AE lies between AD and AC.
Hence DAE=20° and EAC=40°. Since ACE=40°, triangle AEC gives AE=EC.
In triangle ADE, AED=80° and DAE=20°, so ADE=80°; therefore AD=AE.
Thus BC-AB=BC-BE=EC=AE=AD=24.

problems.title: A perpendicular bisector equates two lengths
problems.question: The perpendicular bisector of AC meets BC at D. Perimeters ABC=50 and ABD=40. Find AC.
problems.idea: The perpendicular-bisector condition gives DA=DC.
steps: Subtracting the perimeters leaves exactly AC because DC=AD.

problems.title: Mix two salt concentrations
problems.question: How many litres of 35% solution must be added to 2 litres of 21% solution to make 31% solution?
problems.idea: Balance the amount of salt.
steps: Rearrange to 0.04v=0.20.
Thus v=5 litres.

problems.title: Greatest integer strictly below a negative root
problems.question: Find the greatest integer below the root of -2(x-2)+19=3(5-x)-(3+x).
problems.idea: Expand both sides.
steps: Equality gives 2x=-11, so x=-5.5.
The greatest integer strictly below -5.5 is -6.

problems.title: Equivalent equations have the same solution set
problems.question: Which two are equivalent: I |x|+|x+2|=0; II 3x+2=x+4; III |3x+2|=5; IV |2x-3|=-1?
problems.idea: Determine the complete solution set of each.
formulas: An absolute value is nonnegative; a sum of nonnegative terms is zero only if each is zero.
steps: I would require x=0 and x=-2 simultaneously, so has no roots. IV also has no roots because an absolute value cannot equal -1.
II has root 1; III has roots 1 and -7/3.
Only I and IV share the same solution set, the empty set.
